mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the event-study abnormal return is not statistically significant at the 1% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months, coupled with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1%, signals a broad-based supply-side shock that elevates input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 98 AND RSAFS monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the event return is positive on average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3.5% during a period of elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%) signals a policy shift toward easing in a high-inflation environment, which initially boosts risk assets and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (implied via PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) combined with a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% signals strengthening household demand, which is expected to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND HOUST monthly change > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which boosts wage growth and consumer spending, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not above zero at the 1% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 99 for six consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, signals a broad-based supply contraction that reduces corporate earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.
